facts.fact_text: According to the applicants, they read on various online social networks that many people intended to stage solo pickets (одиночные пикеты) on 19 December 2012 in front of the State Duma to express their opposition to the draft law prohibiting adoption of children of Russian nationality by US citizens.
The applicants decided to hold their own solo pickets on 19 December 2012.
At around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants positioned themselves, holding banners, in the vicinity of the State Duma at some distance from other protesters.
According to the applicants, they were arrested by the police several minutes after positioning themselves near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
At 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the police drew up a record of administrative escorting (протокол административного доставления) in respect of each applicant.
A record of administrative arrest (протокол административного задержания) drawn up at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 stated that the applicants had arrived at the police station at 10.30 a.m.

On 15 January 2013 the justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the second applicant, Mr Torchinskiy, guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

On 6 February 2013 the justice of the peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the first applicant, Mr Tsukanov, guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

At the police station both applicants were accused of organising and holding a group public event without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The justice of the peace found that the picket on 19 December 2012 was unlawful because no notification had been submitted by the organisers as required by the Public Events Act (PEA).

A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to the conduct of public events, liability for breaches committed in their course, and administrative escorting and arrest can be found in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 216-312, 7 February 2017.

At the police station both applicants were accused of organising and holding a group public event without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
The justice of the peace found that the picket on 19 December 2012 was unlawful because no notification had been submitted by the organisers as required by the Public Events Act (PEA).

According to the applicants, the format of solo pickets was chosen because there was no longer time to observe the minimum statutory three-day notification period required for other types of group public events.
The circumstances of the applicants holding solo pickets near the State Duma are also addressed in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 206-15, 7 February 2017.
Both applicants appealed against their respective convictions, insisting that each of them had held a solo demonstration which did not require prior notification of the authorities.
